# tenboards

> A React 19, TanStack Start and Tailwind v4 admin template with reusable shadcn/Base UI blocks, typed demo/database reads and zero-config demo mode.

Generated from registry.json, source blocks, package scripts, adopter guidance and Agent Skills. Do not edit generated assets.

## Install and build

Use Node 22+ and npm. In this repository, import from @/components/blocks and use the generators. External React 19 + Tailwind v4 projects must initialize shadcn first, then run npx shadcn add <absolute-registry-url>. Items include their exact primitive/chart dependencies and the global default light/dark theme, typography, density, focus and motion rules. Review the CSS changes. Installed modules live in components/tenboards; table helpers live in lib/tenboards.

URLs beginning with / are relative to the origin serving this file. Resolve them with new URL(path, llmsUrl).href before passing them to shadcn; for example, resolve /r/stat-card.json against the URL from which you fetched /llms.txt. The kit computes absolute commands from its current browser origin after hydration. No production hostname is baked into installs.

## Blocks

- [DashboardCard](/r/dashboard-card.json): Compact or standard card surface with composable slots.
- [SectionHeader](/r/section-header.json): Semantic card heading with description and wrapping actions.
- [StatCard](/r/stat-card.json): Labelled metric with tabular value, trend and supporting text.
- [CardContent](/r/card-content.json): Content slot with the shared card spacing.
- [PageHeader](/r/page-header.json): Responsive page h1 with description and action slots.
- [DashboardChart](/r/dashboard-chart.json): Responsive Recharts container with series, axis and reduced-motion helpers.
- [DashboardTooltip](/r/dashboard-tooltip.json): Token-colored tooltip preserving named series and value formatting.
- [DashboardLegend](/r/dashboard-legend.json): Wrapping legend with labelled, distinct line patterns.
- [DataTable](/r/data-table.json): Caller-owned TanStack Table v9 with sorting, pagination, mobile reflow and empty state.

## Generators

- npm run new:dashboard <slug>: Metrics and charts; creates /dashboard/<slug>, navigation, guarded loader and typed illustrative demo/database reads.
- npm run new:page <slug>: Listing page; creates /dashboard/<slug>, navigation, guarded loader and typed illustrative demo/database reads.

## Agent Skills

- [tenboards-build-ui](/agent-docs/agents/skills/tenboards-build-ui/SKILL.md): Build tenboards dashboards and app pages with generators and public blocks. Use when adding or changing a dashboard, page, KPI, chart, revenue summary, or data table.
- [tenboards-connect-data](/agent-docs/agents/skills/tenboards-connect-data/SKILL.md): Connect tenboards typed reads to demo fixtures and Postgres with Drizzle. Use when adding a data source, database query, schema migration, seed, parity scenario, or auth-guarded server loader.

## Verification

Run npm run build, npm run check, npm run typecheck and npm run verify:page -- /dashboard/<slug>. Keep fixtures server-side and requireSession() inside each app-data server function. A configured failing database must show an error. Use seriesConfig and useChartMotion for charts and preserve accessible data alternatives.

## Source: AGENTS.md

# Building with tenboards

Maintaining tenboards upstream? Read dev/MAINTAINERS.md first.

## Stack and map

Use Node 22+, npm, strict TypeScript, React 19, TanStack Start (SSR), Tailwind v4,
shadcn/Base UI, TanStack Table v9 and Recharts. Reuse installed dependencies.
Read DESIGN.md for tokens and PRODUCT.md for product context.

- `src/routes/(main)/dashboard/<slug>/`: dashboard and app routes; feature code in `-components/`.
- `src/components/blocks/`: public cards, headings, tables and chart API; `/dashboard/kit` has live examples.
- `src/components/ui/` and `src/components/calendar/`: existing primitives; inspect wrappers, do not edit them to style a page.
- `src/server/data/`: typed demo/database reads and parity registry.
- `src/server/db/`: schema, additive migrations, canonical fixtures and seed.
- `src/navigation/`: sidebar and shared route catalog.
- `scripts/templates/`: generator templates; `docs/data-layer.md` explains database integration.
- `.agents/skills/`: canonical Agent Skills; `.claude/skills/` contains relative mirrors.

## Build loop

1. Use `tenboards-build-ui` for dashboard/page/KPI/chart/table work; use
   `tenboards-connect-data` for database reads, fixtures, migrations and parity.
2. Inspect a local example and the relevant block props before editing.
3. Scaffold with `npm run new:dashboard sales` or `npm run new:page vendors`.
   Both create `/dashboard/<slug>`, navigation/catalog entries, guarded loaders,
   typed reads and illustrative fixtures. Existing slugs are rejected, never overwritten.
4. Adapt the generated types, fixtures and route-local components to the requested
   domain. Import presentation from `@/components/blocks`; chart primitives can
   also come from `@/components/blocks/charts`. Do not rebuild equivalent cards/tables.
5. Keep data behind typed reads and guarded server functions. The generated DB
   implementation is an explicit illustrative stub, not a real database query.
   Use the data skill before connecting live data; never silently fall back on DB errors.
6. Run `npm run build`, `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, then
   `npm run verify:page -- /dashboard/<slug>` (optionally `--base-url http://127.0.0.1:3000`).
   `check` includes `check:design` and `check:skills`. Fix failures and rerun affected checks.
7. Inspect light/dark × desktop/mobile renders, keyboard access and empty states.
   `verify/` reports contain axe and console/hydration results; keep generated evidence out of source commits.

## Invariants

- Use named semantic tokens and spacing/type scales. No raw color literals or
  arbitrary color/size/spacing/type values in page/block code; do not add design exceptions for new pages.
- Preserve compact density: body/table text ≥13px, metadata ≥12px, targets ≥24px;
  keep mobile input text readable and preserve visible focus/reduced motion.
- Use `useChartMotion()` on animated marks and tooltips. Keep series labels and
  an accessible data alternative; color alone must not carry meaning.
- SSR and first client render must match. Serialize a request clock for date-based
  data, or start live clocks after hydration. Browser APIs belong in effects or
  guarded client code; do not add `use client`, disable SSR or suppress hydration errors.
- Route groups such as `(main)` add no URL segment; `route.tsx` defines layouts,
  `$param` names dynamic segments, and `-` files are excluded from route generation.
  Never hand-edit `src/routeTree.gen.ts`; use dev/build or `npm run generate-routes`.
- Keep fixtures server-side; components consume loader data and type-only contracts.
  Every app-data server function calls `requireSession()` independently of the route guard.
- No environment variables are needed for demo mode. A configured failing database
  must produce a visible error. Never put credentials in client code or committed files.

# Design System: tenboards

## Overview

**Creative North Star: "Refined product UI"** — the approved Linear/Vercel register in PLAN §7. Precision, scanability, and restraint serve dense administrative work. PLAN and its Decisions log win every conflict.

The frontmatter records the v0.6.2 compact desktop defaults (mobile controls and spacing retain the larger rhythm). The default combines cool neutral surfaces with a deep blue action accent. Task 007 supplies token-only Graphite, Pine, and Iris alternatives. The v0.1 shell and v0.2 dashboard usages apply these tokens at usage sites; app-page content remains assigned to v0.3.

**Key Characteristics:** neutral-first surfaces, one action accent, crisp borders, compact data, restrained depth, and consistent control states.

## Colors

src/styles/styles.css owns normative light and dark roles. Shadcn background/card/popover map to bg/surface, their foregrounds map to text, and muted/secondary/accent hover surfaces map to surface-raised. Because shadcn uses “accent” for hover fill, action-accent names the saturated primary action color. Border is a decorative separator; border-strong is the accessible input/control edge. Ring is the action color and an opaque 2px outline supplements inherited translucent focus rings.

Supported AA text pairs: text, text-muted (including placeholders), primary, success, warning, danger, and info on each of bg/surface/surface-raised; primary-foreground on primary (including existing 80% hover fills); each semantic foreground on its matching semantic surface. All require 4.5:1, even for large text. Ring and border-strong require 3:1 against all three neutral surfaces. No claim is made for arbitrary cross-role combinations or inherited hard-coded chart/page colors. Low-contrast decorative border is never the sole control boundary.

Run `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-contrast.ts` against the dev server; `--presets` and `--base-url` support later preset/version checks. It resolves rendered CSS values, converts to sRGB, and checks WCAG relative luminance. Disabled controls retain native disabled semantics, pointer suppression, opacity, and cursor treatment; inactive controls are contrast-exempt, and their treatment must not be used for enabled explanatory text. Text selection and input carets use the primary pair.

Presets use only task 005 palette primitives. Default retains blue; Graphite uses charcoal/silver, Pine uses deep teal/mint, and Iris uses violet/lavender. Each changes only primary; all semantic colors, foreground pairings, focus, type, spacing, radii, and shadows inherit the shared contract. The generator resolves each swatch from its referenced root primitive and rejects unresolvable values. No literal palette values live in preset files.

Persisted Tangerine, Brutalist/Neo Brutalism, and Soft Pop selections migrate to Default during boot, before hydration, and their cookie is rewritten. The parser and preference store retain their existing allowed-value fallback; the provider reads the sanitized DOM. Valid new selections and the font registry remain intact. Verify all presets with `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-contrast.ts --presets default,graphite,pine,iris`.

Verified contrast floor (35 supported checks per mode, 2026-10-23; full results in PR evidence):

| Preset | Light text / hover | Dark text / hover | Light control / focus | Dark control / focus |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | 5.30:1 | 7.05:1 | 3.41:1 | 3.70:1 |
| Graphite | 6.11:1 | 7.26:1 | 3.41:1 | 3.70:1 |
| Pine | 4.67:1 | 7.26:1 | 3.41:1 | 3.70:1 |
| Iris | 5.63:1 | 6.79:1 | 3.41:1 | 3.70:1 |


## Typography

Geist Sans and Geist Mono are self-hosted through the approved Fontsource packages. The font registry retains every previous choice; default Geist stylesheets use local assets. Mono is loaded for code/data regardless of the chosen body face. The fixed scale is 12/13/14/16/18/21/26/32px; heading tracking is -0.025em. Tabular numerals are inherited globally so every metric aligns without per-widget edits.

## Layout

Existing screens use responsive grids, compact controls, and route-local components. Compact is the single default, with no density preference. Desktop uses a 3.5px Tailwind spacing unit (formerly 4px): standard cards have 14px internal spacing, small cards retain 12px, default controls are 28px, and page gutters/grid gaps formerly 24px become 21px. Mobile retains the 4px spacing unit, 16px standard card padding and 32px default controls. Interactive button targets have a 24px minimum on both; checkbox/radio/switch hit areas retain the protected primitives’ pseudo-element expansion. Mobile text entry remains 16px to avoid input-focus zoom.

The app surfaces use **Operate** mode. Data density, scanability, native expectations, and consistency outrank expressive decoration. Mobile changes are structural, including the existing sidebar sheet and collapsing grids.

## Elevation & Depth

Cards preserve their inherited thin border/ring structure. Low elevation uses two subtle offset layers; overlays use wider layered shadows. Shared durations are 150ms and 200ms with standard ease-out; Tailwind transitions default to 150ms. Reduced-motion media rules reduce all animations/transitions to near-instant and disable smooth scrolling. Dashboard composition and JS chart behavior are handled by the shared presentation layer and route-local motion subscriptions.

## Shapes

Default control radius is 8px; shadcn aliases use 4/6/8/12/16/20/24px. Cards use the 12px step. Desktop named spacing primitives are 3.5/7/12/14/21/28px; mobile keeps 4/8/12/16/24/32px. The small-card 12px floor is independent of the 3.5px desktop utility rhythm. The floating sidebar uses the 24px radius step, larger than dense controls.

## Components

The original tenboards identity uses a paired-board “10” silhouette and a Geist wordmark. In the app, the mark inherits currentColor and is decorative beside the wordmark or a named link; isolated SVG assets carry their own accessible name. Favicons use the tested white-on-blue primary pair. The SVG wordmark master is dark-on-light; use the inherited-color React wordmark in dark UI. Metadata assets and vector masters are documented in README.

Use local Base UI-backed shadcn wrappers after inspecting their source. Button variants include primary, outline, secondary, ghost, destructive, and link; focus uses a border plus ring. Inputs have focus, invalid, disabled, and placeholder states. Cards use semantic card foreground/background with header/content/footer slots. Chips and navigation should share the semantic palette.

The locked sidebar reference is [docs/design-refs/sidebar-reference.png](docs/design-refs/sidebar-reference.png), inspected for this document. The implemented shell uses its inset floating rounded panel, workspace avatar/name and collapse control, search pill with ⌘K, regular-weight primary items with outline icons, soft gray active pills, secondary collapsible sections, pinned status card, and footer actions. Expanded navigation is 18rem wide; icon-collapse is 4.5rem. The panel sits 12px from desktop viewport edges; on mobile the sheet panel itself is inset 8px from the viewport, with 40px mobile rows and 18px icons (36px rows and 16px icons on desktop), 12px active pills, and a sticky viewport-height wrapper. Home, Projects, Email and Chat precede the project disclosures and Dashboards, Pages and Misc sections; AI Assistant follows Chat. The demo card counts visited enabled concrete dashboard destinations, including project views and excluding aliases, since the sidebar mounted; footer actions are Settings, Help, Documentation, and Feedback.

The header is 48px tall on desktop and 56px on mobile, with linked Projects/project ancestor breadcrumbs and a current-view label on project pages, a truncating current-page label elsewhere, theme/settings/account controls, and a link to the tenboards repository. The Workspace prefix and repository link are hidden below 640px. The header sidebar trigger appears on mobile and when desktop off-canvas navigation is hidden. Desktop icon rails retain only their own sidebar toggle; the breadcrumb starts at the normal header padding. Expanded desktop navigation keeps its sidebar toggle. If a focused header opener becomes hidden, focus transfers to the sidebar toggle. Desktop search lives in the sidebar; below 768px the header gets a compact search trigger. The account menu uses clearly labeled demo identities with initials avatars.

The root command palette uses the existing cmdk and dialog wrappers and the shared retained-route catalog. Search rows are at least 35px tall on desktop and 40px on mobile; the result list scrolls within a bounded viewport. The dialog has a title, description, explicit search label, empty state, and a touch close button. ⌘K/Ctrl+K toggles the palette, including inside text fields. Alt/Shift, key repeat, IME composition, already-handled events, and another visible dialog/menu/listbox suppress the shortcut (the mobile navigation sheet excepted). The search input group uses one opaque 2px focus outline with 2px offset and 8px corners; the inner input outline is suppressed. Keyboard selection, Escape, and focus return are part of the component contract.

Layout settings is a right-hand sheet capped at 28rem on desktop and full width on mobile. Appearance and Layout sections group native labeled selects and fieldset radio choices. Controls are at least 35px tall on desktop and 40px on mobile; the body scrolls independently of its heading and reset footer. Selected choices use a neutral fill and 1px primary border; keyboard focus adds an opaque 2px outline with 2px offset. The Defaults footer derives all seven labels from the registry. Existing seven-day preference cookies and the separate sidebar-state cookie remain the layout persistence contract; Reset also re-expands the sidebar. The visible variant/mobile explanations describe the supported sidebar adaptations.

## Do's and Don'ts

- Do use Impeccable and read its craft floor immediately before UI edits.
- Do preserve semantic shadcn compatibility, font choices, SSR, and preference behavior.
- Do verify rendered light/dark desktop/mobile states and contrast with evidence.
- Don't redesign dashboard or app-page content in v0.1.
- Don't treat documentation of a future design as proof it is implemented.
- Don't remove screens or copy third-party logos into the tenboards identity.


## Dashboard presentation foundation

`@/components/blocks` exports the public `DashboardCard`, `SectionHeader`, and `StatCard` APIs from `src/components/blocks/cards.tsx`. Compact/standard density maps to 12/14px desktop card spacing (12/16px on mobile); headings are semantic h2/h3, labels wrap and metric values use tabular numerals. Optional help, trend and action slots retain route-owned data and behavior. The completed v0.2 implementation reuses these primitives across all 14 current/legacy dashboard routes; domain values and interactions stay local.

`src/components/blocks/charts.tsx` composes protected chart exports, available through `@/components/blocks`. Use `DashboardChart` for bounded responsive height and visible keyboard focus, `chartAxis` for 12px muted ticks, `chartGrid` for decorative dashed separators, `chartCursor`, `DashboardTooltip`, and wrapping `DashboardLegend`. `seriesConfig` deliberately selects chart-1/2/4/5 (primary, text-muted, success, warning) rather than duplicate Default chart-3. Every line also needs a distinct dash/marker or labeled form; multi-series charts use solid/dashed/dotted series with matching line samples, direct labels or accessible data tables. Marks use opaque token strokes, with area fills only as supplementary cues. Numeric formatters use explicit en-US locale; route code owns time ranges and units.

Pass `useChartMotion()` to every animated series and tooltip. Its server snapshot and initial hydration disable animation, then a guarded media-query subscription observes changes and permits 200ms animation only when reduced motion is off. No global tokens, font/preset registry or protected wrappers change.


The integrated dashboard layout uses equal-height cards within a common comparison row; stacked auxiliary columns align their outer bounds where they share that row. Independent work streams such as Productivity's main work and calendar/notes sidebar keep their content-driven heights. Tables scroll locally or reflow to labelled mobile fields; no data is hidden to fit.

Patient Monitoring retains local simulation and signal identity: labelled ECG/success, Pleth/info, Resp/warning and ART/danger traces. Continuous subscriptions pause under reduced motion, while numeric readings and a post-hydration live UTC clock remain available. Static date-based dashboards explicitly identify their deterministic demo reporting dates; no hydration warning suppression or page SSR removal is used.


The public `DataTable` accepts a caller-owned TanStack Table v9 instance configured with `dataTableFeatures`. Shared sort buttons, Previous/Next controls, row counts and an empty slot compose the protected table/button primitives. Labelled mobile fields retain all visible columns; the optional scroll mode preserves tabular layout. Column definitions and server/client state remain outside the block. Specialized route tables retain their existing layouts.

`/dashboard/kit` uses Operate mode and the established compact tokens. A single PageHeader, fragment-link navigation and separated example sections expose the blocks, their variants and static source. Examples use the live compiled modules as their copyable source. No tokens, presets or protected primitives change.

## App-page headings

`src/components/blocks/page-header.tsx`, exported through `@/components/blocks`, owns the small `PageHeader` presentation API: required string `title`, optional string `description`, React `actions`, and optional layout `className`. The h1 uses the 21px scale with medium weight and tight tracking; descriptive text uses the muted 13px role. A wrapping flex row, shrinkable title column and wrapping action slot support narrow screens and long titles. File Manager and Products consume it first; Tasks and Invoice follow in their owned tasks. It owns no route, state or data. Continue using `SectionHeader` for card h2/h3 semantics and the existing dashboard primitives for cards.

## Compact density contract (v0.6.2)

The browser rem root remains 16px. Body content and tables use 13px/18px; the previously unstyled body fallback was 16px/24px while normal content was 14px/20px. Metadata/labels never go below 12px. SectionHeader uses 14px/20px; page headings use 21px/28px; StatCard values use 21px, rising to 26px on wide desktops (formerly 24/30px). The inherited 18px `text-lg` step is now explicitly 16px, and 36px `text-4xl` is 32px. Heading tracking, weights, colors, focus outlines and reduced-motion behavior are unchanged.

This targets about 8–12% overall desktop compaction, rather than scaling every pixel uniformly: normal text shrinks 7%, most spacing 12.5%, KPI values 13%, sidebar rows 10%, and the desktop header 14%. Floors and intentional exceptions take precedence. Chart containers, FullCalendar and date-picker geometry keep their original spacing context and rem-based sizing; chart ticks stay 12px. Sidebar widths and breakpoints stay unchanged to protect long labels. Mobile adopts the type hierarchy but keeps larger control/card spacing and its 56px header.

Toolbar selects and tabs keep a content-based minimum width, including their icons and gaps, instead of clipping wider font choices into fixed compact widths. Full-width form selects retain their responsive wrapping layout; Calendar switches to intrinsic width on desktop. The 24px control floor lives in the base layer so larger minimums at usage sites remain effective.


## Assistant

The Assistant uses Operate mode at compact density. A full-height page holds a centered 752px conversation with an independently scrolling message area. User messages are compact right-aligned muted bubbles; assistant replies have a small Bot icon and left-aligned generative UI. A centered welcome block offers three suggestion cards in a two-column grid. Illustrative replies are identified in one short line.

The composer stays below the scroll area, with mobile safe-area spacing. Its textarea grows from one to eight rows, keeps a hidden Message label, and supports Enter to send and Shift+Enter for a newline. A compact provider/model select (or subtle Recorded demo badge) shares the bottom toolbar with the icon Send/Stop button. Focus returns to the composer on send, stop, regeneration and clear. Session expiration focuses Sign in to continue.

The read-only registry uses DashboardCard/StatCard, compact Table rows and the existing chart components. Table/chart groups have card frames; nested frames are flattened at the usage site. Charts retain keyboard access, tabular alternatives and reduced-motion handling. Supported semantic token pairs are reused, with no new tokens, fonts or presets.

The message log is polite and marked busy during streaming; a separate status announces lifecycle changes. The initial streaming placeholder has reduced-motion-aware dots. Scrolling follows only within 160px of the bottom and pauses when reading older messages; Jump to latest resumes following. Regenerate and Copy reply are small, named icon controls with tooltips under the latest assistant turn. Clipboard failures provide inline recovery. New conversation explains transient retention in a tooltip.

Recovery remains inline: bounded-context notices in the transcript; input errors and Retry-After near the composer; explicit provider recovery and session-expiration focus. No request, auth, limiter, stream validation or provider behavior changes in the visual refinement.

## Projects workspace usage (v0.8)

The workspace uses Operate mode at the v0.6.2 compact scale. Shared StatCards present Home/Overview metrics; existing Select and segmented ToggleGroup controls serve filters, Timeline modes/scales and Files display. No token, preset, font or density registry changes accompany Projects. Semantic status dots and priority icons pair color with text, short task keys aid scanning, and initials use the existing Avatar circles. Empty counters are omitted from Board cards; task details retain a focused dialog and keyboard return.

The project header has one project-qualified shell breadcrumb, a compact selector, status, member avatars and progress. Overview uses member rows and request-relative due labels. Timeline preserves visible text/date cues alongside semantic bars, today marker, bounded scrolling range and collapsible unscheduled work; mobile defaults to Table after safe hydration. Calendar geometry and protected adapters are unchanged. File metadata uses local file-type/star/share icons without mutation affordances.

Primary Home/Projects precede Email/Chat and Assistant when present; Default remains under Dashboards. Project disclosures contain indented route links with an exact active child. Rail popovers expose the project name and all five links, dismiss on route resolution including same-path navigation, and return focus on Escape. Expansion state lives above the mobile sheet lifetime. The bounded `tenboards:project-nav:v1` localStorage preference restores after hydration and respects manual collapse within a project. Existing keyboard focus, reduced motion, supported semantic token pairs and sidebar layout preferences are preserved.


## Source: docs/data-layer.md

# Optional local data layer

v0.4 is released. Production and version previews remain demonstration Workers;
Neon hosting and Hyperdrive belong to v0.6. v0.5 adds optional local authentication
on this database source; see [the auth guide](auth.md). Business-data forms,
selection, drag/reorder, alarm acknowledgement, invoice edits and message controls
remain local demonstrations. Auth forms and account/session controls persist real
auth records when a private secret enables local auth. No read function writes data, authorizes a
user, establishes a session, sends a message or connects a medical feed.

## Start without a database

Use Node 22+ and npm in a clean checkout:

```sh
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000/dashboard/default`. With no `.env`, `DATABASE_URL` or
`DATA_SOURCE`, this works with Docker stopped. `npm run build` also needs no DB.
The dev script uses Node's `--env-file-if-exists=.env`; inherited shell variables
still take precedence. To return to demo after setting up a DB, set
`DATA_SOURCE=demo` in the shell or local `.env`, or remove the DB configuration.
Also unset `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`: a nonempty secret requires the real DB source and
intentionally rejects forced demo or a missing DB.

## Opt into Postgres 17

Docker Compose is optional. From the repository root:

```sh
docker compose up -d
cp .env.example .env
npm run db:migrate
npm run db:seed
npm run data:parity
npm run dev
```

Copy the example only when creating a new local `.env`; preserve an existing file.
It contains only local development credentials. The Compose service binds to
loopback port 54329 and uses database/user `tenboards`, password `tenboards_local`.
Never commit `.env` or production credentials. There is no hosted DB provisioning.
Migrate and seed are explicit commands; development startup never performs either.
Wait for `docker compose ps` to show the database healthy if starting from a cold
image. A failed read is visible and can be retried after repairing configuration.

Stop the container with `docker compose stop`; resume with `docker compose up -d`.
The named volume preserves local records. This guide intentionally provides no
volume-deletion/reset command. Review and back up local data before any manual
cleanup. Reseeding is not an arbitrary database reset.

## Selection and errors

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` absent, `DATA_SOURCE` absent | Demo, without constructing a DB client |
| Valid `DATABASE_URL`, `DATA_SOURCE` absent | Actual Postgres reads |
| `DATA_SOURCE=demo` | Demo, even with an invalid/unreachable configured URL |
| Any other configured `DATA_SOURCE`, including empty | Explicit unsupported-source error |
| Empty/malformed `DATABASE_URL` | Safe visible DB load error; no fallback |
| Connection refused, invalid password, missing migrations | Safe visible DB load error; no fallback |
| Corrected DB configuration/schema | Reads recover on retry/reload |

The selector is `src/server/data/source.ts`. Driver errors, SQL and credentials are
discarded before reaching the browser. The local DB command scripts additionally
reject non-localhost targets. They fail nonzero with a redacted error. Do not infer
that a page is using Postgres merely because a URL exists: forced demo wins.

## Read boundary and ownership

Each route calls a GET TanStack Start server function from its loader. Server
handlers independently require the actual session in auth mode before importing
`src/server/data/<domain>.ts`; components receive serializable
loader data through typed props or a route-local context. Domain modules expose
`readX`, `demoX` and `dbX`; the selector chooses the actual implementation. DB client
construction and queries are lazy and server-only. Components/state stores never
import runtime seed fixtures. Types, pure arithmetic, icons, styling, navigation,
form choices, chart geometry and preference registries remain UI code.

| Module / exported read | Consumers and records |
| --- | --- |
| `accounts` / `readAccounts` | Demo shell accounts; auth-on header uses the real session identity instead |
| `users` / `readUsers` | Directory, workspaces and memberships |
| `roles` / `readRoles` | Informational roles and ordered permissions |
| `profile` / `readProfile` | Six Profile tabs, contact/employment/documents/time off |
| `products` / `readProducts` | Product catalog, categories and status options |
| `invoices` / `readInvoices` | Parties, taxes, items and request-relative draft dates |
| `ecommerce` / `readEcommerce` | Store orders, reviews, products, inventory and metrics |
| `kanban` / `readKanban` | Board/list/table records, columns, owners and summaries |
| `tasks` / `readTasks` | Separate task ledger |
| `files` / `readFiles` | Folders/files, owners/shares and summaries |
| `calendar` / `readCalendar` | Typed relative event definitions |
| `mail` / `readMail` | Standalone Mail and dashboard iframe; accounts/messages/attachments |
| `chat` / `readChat` | Standalone Chat and dashboard iframe; contacts/messages/reactions |
| `default` / `readDefault` | Customer dashboard |
| `crm` / `readCrm` | Opportunities dashboard |
| `finance` / `readFinance` | Accounts/cards/transactions and metrics |
| `analytics` / `readAnalytics` | Visitor/page/source/campaign models |
| `productivity` / `readProductivity` | Tasks/projects/notes/goals/focus/quote and civil day |
| `academy` / `readAcademy` | Classes/rooms/schedules/assignments/events/achievements |
| `logistics` / `readLogistics` | Customers/shipments/cargo/tracking/handling/locations |
| `infrastructure` / `readInfrastructure` | Organizations/projects/environments/resources |
| `patients` / `readPatients` | Beds/identities/clinical baselines/alarms/events/settings |

There are 22 registered reads and 104 parity scenarios. v0.6.1 removes 26 V1-only scenarios: Default 8, CRM 6, Finance 6 and Analytics 6. Retained screen coverage is unchanged. Auth/system/error
routes and redirects have no persisted app-domain data. Mail/Chat dashboard aliases
load their standalone source through iframes. The shared dashboard account loader
also covers non-data dashboard states.

## Schema, fixtures and seed

Plain modules under `src/server/db/fixtures/` are the single canonical seed source.
Natural entities and ordered relations have domain tables and foreign keys. Similar
names never imply a shared identity: shell accounts, directory users, profile,
commerce customers, proposals/leads and workspace tasks are distinct universes.
No whole-fixture JSON payload table is used.

Aggregates use `metric_points`: domain, series, point key, position, decimal value,
unit and optional currency. Ordered dimensions preserve labels and exact display
format metadata; they are not hidden copies of entire business objects. Numeric
parts of formatted KPIs stay numeric, including grouped currency, percentages,
ratios and durations. Short illustrative lists deliberately need not reconcile to
aggregate totals. Infrastructure's header totals, for example, are independent of
its small visible environment sample.

The transactional seed upserts known stable keys, refreshes owned ordered children
and metric dimensions, and preserves unrelated parent records. Repeating it is
stable. Editing a seeded record locally is temporary: reseeding restores the
canonical value for that key. Removing a fixture from source does not authorize a
global delete; add an explicit, reviewed migration/cleanup policy if needed.

All reads specify deterministic ordering, with stable keys as tie breakers where
applicable. Postgres numeric values convert deliberately at DTO boundaries;
coordinates retain ten fractional digits in storage, and parity checks the exact
original JavaScript numbers. Money/metric formatting is explicit, not dependent on
the server locale. Optional fields remain absent where the original contract used
absence; missing lookups return the domain's documented null/empty result. Missing
required related records are errors, never silently replaced by fixture values.

## Dates and live simulation

Civil dates use ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`; fixed labels explicitly format UTC. Calendar,
Invoice and Mail store typed offsets/definitions and resolve one serialized
request reference on each read. Seeding never bakes today's rendered dates into
those definitions. Calendar adopts browser-local month/wall time after hydration;
Today and its now marker keep the real clock. Month-end CRM labels preserve
clamped month subtraction.

Patient Monitoring alone retains client-simulated waveform/trend/tick computation
in `waveform-data.ts`, `realtime-utils.ts`, `use-patient-vital-series.ts` and
`use-realtime-tick.ts`. Their geometry, calibration/axis labels, deterministic
initial samples and live tick mechanics are presentation/simulation. Patient
identity, diagnosis, baseline vitals, signal amplitude/phase/rhythm, alarms,
thresholds and settings still come from the read. Reduced motion pauses traces;
it does not freeze the real clock or hide numeric readings. No ordinary chart
series or “realtime visitors” snapshot is exempt.

## Migrations and validation

`npm run db:generate` generates SQL and journal metadata from the schema.
Review generated SQL, commit it, and apply `npm run db:migrate`; never regenerate
an older migration to change history. The stack journal is linear and cumulative.

| Layer | Cumulative SQL migrations |
| --- | --- |
| 001 | `0000_cynical_solo.sql`, `0001_flaky_the_santerians.sql` |
| 002 | `0002_nice_gideon.sql`, `0003_smiling_tombstone.sql` |
| 003 | `0004_easy_la_nuit.sql` |
| 004 | `0005_abandoned_red_ghost.sql` |
| 005 | `0006_useful_quentin_quire.sql` |
| 006 | `0007_even_the_santerians.sql`, `0008_cultured_praxagora.sql`, `0009_large_katie_power.sql` |
| 007 | `0010_plain_thunderball.sql` |
| 008 | `0011_blushing_siren.sql` |

For an existing checkout, update code, run migrate, then seed. A second generate on
unchanged schema must report no changes.

`npm run data:parity` invokes separate demo and actual DB implementations with
identical inputs/context, compares exact results/types/order and verifies caller
mutation cannot contaminate subsequent reads. Its inventory matches every exported
`readX` function; omissions, DB failures and mismatches fail nonzero. It covers
missing IDs, filters, later request times after seed, leap days,
year/month rollover and date ranges. Negative controls:

```sh
npm run data:parity -- --inject-mismatch
npm run data:parity -- --omit-registration
```

Both intentionally fail. `node --env-file=.env --experimental-strip-types scripts/data-source-check.ts` checks selection/faults and a TCP sentinel with every
read in forced demo. Its missing-schema test expects a separate empty local
`tenboards_missing_schema` database. `scripts/data-source-browser.ts <output>`
checks visible refused/password/schema errors, forced demo and recovery. Test
credentials and expected errors belong in local evidence, never production config.

Run build, check and typecheck for each change. The capture harness uses the route
manifest and exact downloaded font assets; `--reference <ISO>` sends
`x-tenboards-qa-reference` only to the app origin. Date-relative GET handlers validate
this read-only input and serialize it through the normal DTO. Missing or malformed
headers use real request time. It does not replace Date, pause ticks or change
Today. The incumbent comparison worktree receives the same narrow capture seam;
its business code remains at layer 006 (`474a29e`). Layer 007 separately proved
all 40 operational before/demo/DB image pairs identical, and the final full-catalog
comparison includes those routes in every preset. `--mask-live-clocks` covers only
Patient Monitoring's `[data-monitoring-clock]`. `--hydration-delay-ms 1500 --reload`
and `--timezone` exercise real hydration and refresh in opposite zones.

`node --experimental-strip-types scripts/report-route-coverage.ts --root <evidence> --environments dev,db,workers --retries <manifest.json>` verifies all 608 cases per
source without discarding original failures. `scripts/audit-data-layer.ts` checks
all 22 canonical fixture owners and the transitive runtime import boundary;
companion literal/array inspection classifies UI configuration and client signals.
Chat's final audit correction owns its previously inline three tab counts and
thread date, extending the original communication domain through migration 0011.

For capture reports, failures are retained alongside explicit
reruns. Evidence is committed only to `pr-assets`, never application branches.

## Add a domain

1. Inspect the incumbent records and consumers; separate UI config/types first.
2. Define normalized entity/child tables or typed aggregate metrics. Preserve the
   original keys, relationships, ordering, precision and null semantics.
3. Move canonical plain records to one fixture module; extend the transactional
   seed without deleting unrelated data. Generate the next migration.
4. Implement typed demo/DB/read functions with equivalent inputs, validation and
   output. Queries must actually load the owned tables.
5. Register every read and supported variant/filter/date/missing scenario; prove
   parity against fresh and cumulatively upgraded Postgres.
6. Connect GET server functions/loaders and typed UI data; preserve local actions.
7. Run zero-env/fault/Workers gates and inspect before/demo/DB four-state captures.
   Update README, ownership documentation and review status.

## Hosted database boundary

The only Worker binding remains ASSETS. Demo never constructs a Postgres client,
and browser bundles exclude the driver and credentials. v0.4 adds no Cloudflare
DB secret, binding, Neon instance, Hyperdrive pool or production persistence. A
future hosted integration must separately define credentials, pooling, deployment,
authentication/authorization and operational safeguards. Do not treat local seed
commands or the public demo UI as production administration tools.

## Auth tables and preserved domain ownership

Migration `0012_watery_sugar_man.sql` appends four isolated auth tables after v0.4's
unchanged `0011`. Auth is optional: DB without a secret remains open; a secret adds
route and callable-function session enforcement. Domain reads still have no writes
or identity selection and CLI parity calls them without an HTTP session. All 22
reads remain; v0.6.1 reduces 130 baseline scenarios to 104 by removing only retired V1 coverage. Sample directory roles and
Profile employment data are not authorization or account records. Seeds never
create passwords/auth users and preserve existing auth records. Auth mutations go
through Better Auth and never update these business tables.

## Workers connection lifetime (v0.6 task 001)

Data reads use the same effective request environment as authentication. A valid
`HYPERDRIVE.connectionString` takes precedence over `DATABASE_URL`; an invalid
binding cannot fall through to a valid URL. `DATA_SOURCE=demo` remains connection
free. Workers reuse a client only within one request (max 1); Node retains its
lazy pool (max 4) and explicit CLI shutdown. Worker request cleanup closes sockets,
while Hyperdrive owns hosted pooling. Do not infer hosted TLS or cache correctness
from the local emulator. See [local runtime and tests](auth.md#local-workers-runtime-v06-task-001).

Nitro defaults `cloudflare.nodeCompat` to true and already emitted `nodejs_compat`
before v0.6. The root Wrangler source now states that intent explicitly. Nitro
merges overrides, configured Wrangler values, source config and defaults using
`defu` (arrays can survive/merge); generated output retains date `2026-10-23`,
`index.mjs`, ASSETS and ESModule rules. Never edit generated output. The local
test config explicitly selects `local`; the independent preview source config
selects `tenboards-preview` and cannot inherit root production bindings.

## Direct operational targets

Migration/seed keep their explicit local-only default. Reviewer Neon operations
require `npm run db:migrate -- --allow-remote` and `npm run db:seed -- --allow-remote`,
with a direct TLS DATABASE_URL supplied privately. The target validator rejects
missing/duplicate TLS settings, known pooler endpoints and Hyperdrive binding input.
Parity/auth suites remain local-only. These commands apply additive migrations and
idempotent fixture upserts; they do not reset schemas or create default auth users.
See [the deployment runbook](deploy.md) for ordering, backup/recovery and cutover.

## v0.6.1 legacy cleanup

`0014_remove_legacy.sql` is a new migration after the unchanged shipped journal. It drops 13 tables used exclusively by V1 screens: four CRM tables, two Finance tables, three Analytics V1 tables, two Default V1 tables, `default_proposal_reviewers` and `analytics_coverage_assignments`. It deletes `v1.%` series only for the four core dashboard domains, removing dependent metric dimensions before points. Shared metric tables and all current-screen data remain.

The four core reads no longer accept a variant or return/load V1 payloads. V1 fixtures, seed statements, route server functions and range-specific projectors are deleted. Shared civil-date helpers used by Academy and Productivity remain.

`node --experimental-strip-types scripts/auth-migration-check.ts` creates and drops test-owned databases for fresh and populated upgrade paths from `f45e813`. It compares retained rows, verifies all 13 tables and V1 metric rows are gone, repeats migrations/seed, and runs 22-read/104-scenario parity on each. This migration intentionally deletes retired template data; take a backup before upgrading an adopted installation that may contain customized V1 data.


## Source: docs/deploy.md

# Deploy with your own database

Connect your fork to Neon through Cloudflare Hyperdrive, then publish a complete
Worker with email/password authentication and shared sample data. Allow about
15 minutes once your Cloudflare and Neon accounts are ready; account setup and
build time can add to that. You need Node 22+, npm and a private Bash terminal.

This repository's own live demo intentionally stays in demo mode.

The Hyperdrive→Postgres runtime path is verified **locally in workerd only**.
Hosted Neon TLS/pooling, Cloudflare proxy behavior and remote caching have not
been verified by this project; you verify them for your deployment below.

## Quick path

Replace every `<placeholder>` with your own value. The numbered details below
follow this same order and explain the safety checks.

1. Fork, clone and run `npm ci`; set `name` in `wrangler.jsonc` to `<worker-name>`.
   Log in with `npx wrangler login`. If this Worker is new, create a binding-free,
   secret-free Hello World Worker with that name in the Cloudflare dashboard first.
2. Create a Neon project; copy its **direct**, non-pooled TLS connection URL.
3. Privately run `wrangler hyperdrive create` with `--caching-disabled` (command below).
4. Put the returned nonsecret ID in the source `wrangler.jsonc` HYPERDRIVE binding.
5. Run `db:migrate` and `db:seed` against the direct Neon URL with `-- --allow-remote`.
6. Prepare your clean build and private secrets file:

   ```bash
   set +x
   umask 077
   export TENBOARDS_OPS_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tenboards-deploy.XXXXXX")"
   npm run deploy:prepare -- --name '<worker-name>' \
     --url 'https://<worker-name>.<account-subdomain>.workers.dev' \
     --secrets-file "$TENBOARDS_OPS_DIR/worker-secrets.json"
   ```

7. Inspect your existing version/secret inventory, then follow the helper's printed
   commands: one `versions upload --secrets-file`, inspect/check that candidate,
   and `versions deploy <candidate>@100%` only after it passes.
8. Run `npm run deploy:check -- https://<worker-name>.<account-subdomain>.workers.dev`.
9. Optionally enable OAuth later; keep a compatible rollback version and a separate
   database recovery point.

**Never set secrets on a binding-less live version. Never run your hosted database
with auth off.** Do not use `wrangler secret put`, `secret bulk` or `npm run deploy`
as an intermediate setup step: they can change live traffic before code, binding
and secrets are ready together. Keep automatic deployment disabled during setup.

## 1. Fork and name your Worker

Fork this repository, clone your fork, and install its pinned tooling:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<your-account>/<your-fork>.git
cd <your-fork>
npm ci
npx wrangler login
```

Change only the `name` field in source `wrangler.jsonc` to your chosen Worker name.
Keep `nodejs_compat`, `workers_dev` and `preview_urls` enabled. Find your account's
workers.dev subdomain in Cloudflare Workers & Pages; your canonical origin will be
`https://<worker-name>.<account-subdomain>.workers.dev`. Social metadata defaults to
`/og.png`; for crawlers requiring an absolute URL, set `APP_CONFIG.meta.image` in
`src/config/app-config.ts` to your origin plus `/og.png`.

The pinned Wrangler requires an existing Worker for `versions upload`. For a new
name, use Cloudflare Workers & Pages → Create application → Hello World, choose
that name and deploy the placeholder **without bindings or secrets**. This only
establishes the Worker; it does not expose database data. Do not attach Hyperdrive
or auth secrets in the dashboard. If the Worker already exists, retain its current
known-good version and inspect its bindings/secrets before changing anything.

Use a private session with `set +x` and `umask 077`. Never paste credentials into
Git, PRs, chat, shell history, screenshots or public logs. Wrangler errors may
include configuration details; inspect logs privately and share redacted facts.

## 2. Create Neon and copy its direct URL

Create your Neon project, database and role in your chosen region. In its Connect
dialog disable connection pooling and copy the direct Postgres URL, including
`sslmode=require`. Do not use the `-pooler` hostname. Before changing an existing
database, verify its migration history/schema and create a recovery point or Neon
branch; seeding upserts the template's shared sample records.

Read the URL without echoing it or putting it in shell history:

```bash
set +x
umask 077
read -r -s -p 'Neon direct TLS URL: ' TENBOARDS_DIRECT_DATABASE_URL
```

## 3. Create Hyperdrive with caching disabled

```bash
npx wrangler hyperdrive create '<worker-name>-database' \
  --connection-string "$TENBOARDS_DIRECT_DATABASE_URL" \
  --caching-disabled --sslmode require --update-config=false
npx wrangler hyperdrive get <hyperdrive-id>
```

The expanded connection argument is sensitive; run this privately and do not
publish raw command logs. Confirm the returned configuration has caching disabled:
query caching is unsafe for sessions and revocation. Local emulation ignores the
remote cache setting. See [Cloudflare's Neon setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/hyperdrive/examples/connect-to-postgres/postgres-database-providers/neon/)
and [Hyperdrive configuration](https://developers.cloudflare.com/hyperdrive/get-started/).

## 4. Add the binding ID to source configuration

Replace the commented slot in `wrangler.jsonc` with the real 32-hex ID:

```jsonc
"hyperdrive": [{ "binding": "HYPERDRIVE", "id": "<hyperdrive-id>" }]
```

Add the separating comma after `preview_urls`. The ID is nonsecret and may be
committed. Never commit the connection URL, secrets or `localConnectionString`.
Do not put `DATABASE_URL` in Worker secrets or DB/auth/provider values in `vars`;
the binding supplies the runtime connection. Keep OAuth pairs absent for launch.

## 5. Migrate and seed directly

```bash
DATABASE_URL="$TENBOARDS_DIRECT_DATABASE_URL" npm run db:migrate -- --allow-remote
DATABASE_URL="$TENBOARDS_DIRECT_DATABASE_URL" npm run db:seed -- --allow-remote
unset TENBOARDS_DIRECT_DATABASE_URL
```

Remote commands require explicit opt-in, a direct URL and TLS. They reject known
pooling endpoints; do not migrate through Hyperdrive. Repeating both commands is
safe: migrations track history and seeds transactionally upsert fixtures without
resetting schemas or adding default auth accounts. Existing auth identities stay
separate from sample directory users. Verify the intended database before each
run; auth grants access to shared data, not tenancy or per-user business ownership.

## 6. Prepare the build and secrets

Run the `deploy:prepare` command in the quick path from your repository root.
Move local `.env*` and `.dev.vars*` files outside the repository first (keep
`.env.example`). The helper filters inherited environment variables, rejects
local dotenv/dev-vars inputs and builds without credentials. It checks the
**generated** `.output/server/wrangler.json` against `--name`, requires
`nodejs_compat` and exactly one HYPERDRIVE binding with a nonzero 32-hex ID, and
rejects `localConnectionString` and DB/auth/provider vars. It cannot verify that
an ID exists or that remote caching is disabled; that is step 3.

`--url` is required and must be your exact public HTTPS origin. With
`--secrets-file`, the helper creates a new file outside the repository with mode
0600 containing a random `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` and your `BETTER_AUTH_URL`. It never
prints the secret values, follows no existing destination symlink, and refuses to
overwrite a file. Its parent directory must already exist. The helper contacts
neither Cloudflare nor a database; it only builds, validates and prints next commands.

On later deployments, **omit `--secrets-file` to build/validate without generating
new secrets** and use your existing private file in the upload command. Do not
rotate your auth secret accidentally. Store it in your private secret manager;
remove the temporary file when you finish. A new secret can invalidate sessions.

Always select `.output/server/wrangler.json` for the following commands; Nitro
provides the entry, assets and module settings. Never hand-edit generated output
or use root `wrangler.jsonc` as the deployment entry. Prepare afresh after any
source change or preview build.

## 7. Upload one complete version, check it, then promote

Record your known-good version before proceeding:

```bash
export TENBOARDS_DEPLOY_CONFIG='.output/server/wrangler.json'
npx wrangler deployments list --config "$TENBOARDS_DEPLOY_CONFIG"
npx wrangler versions list --config "$TENBOARDS_DEPLOY_CONFIG"
npx wrangler secret list --config "$TENBOARDS_DEPLOY_CONFIG"
npx wrangler versions view <known-good-version-id> --config "$TENBOARDS_DEPLOY_CONFIG" --json
```

For first setup, the existing placeholder/demo must have no database binding or
secrets. Abort if inventories are unexpected. Later, preserve the existing auth
secret pair and compatible binding. Secrets omitted from an upload file are
preserved, so inspect the prior inventory rather than assuming it is empty.
[Cloudflare documents atomic code/secret upload](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/secrets/#upload-secrets-alongside-code).

```bash
npx wrangler versions upload --config "$TENBOARDS_DEPLOY_CONFIG" \
  --secrets-file "$TENBOARDS_OPS_DIR/worker-secrets.json"
read -r -p 'Candidate version ID: ' TENBOARDS_CANDIDATE_VERSION
read -r -p 'Candidate immutable origin: ' TENBOARDS_CANDIDATE_ORIGIN
npx wrangler versions view "$TENBOARDS_CANDIDATE_VERSION" --config "$TENBOARDS_DEPLOY_CONFIG" --json
npm run deploy:check -- "$TENBOARDS_CANDIDATE_ORIGIN"
```

Use the full version ID and immutable URL returned by Wrangler. Confirm the
candidate has ASSETS, your real HYPERDRIVE ID and exactly the two launch auth secret
names, with no OAuth or direct DB URL. The candidate uses your **canonical** origin
for auth, not its version URL; do not run signup or `--auth-roundtrip` on the
candidate origin. Version URLs share bindings and data; they are not isolated PR
previews. Stop if any check fails. After success, promote the whole version:

```bash
npx wrangler versions deploy "$TENBOARDS_CANDIDATE_VERSION@100%" \
  --config "$TENBOARDS_DEPLOY_CONFIG" --yes
```

Do not split traffic between a demo and authenticated code. Never create a hybrid
with auth/no binding (503) or binding/no auth (public data). Keep code, binding and
both auth secrets together, including later rotations or OAuth additions.

## 8. Check your live deployment

```bash
npm run deploy:check -- 'https://<worker-name>.<account-subdomain>.workers.dev'
# Optional explicit account write, on the canonical origin only:
npm run deploy:check -- 'https://<worker-name>.<account-subdomain>.workers.dev' --auth-roundtrip
```

The default check sends bounded GETs to all four auth forms, public Unauthorized
and 404 pages, the signed-out dashboard redirect and the null private/no-store
session endpoint. It rejects demo/auth-off, unsafe redirects, malformed sessions
and server errors, follows no cross-origin redirects and replays no cookies.
GETs have at most two attempts, eight seconds each; POSTs are never retried.
Requests can update rate-limit counters, but default smoke requests no account or
business-data writes. `--demo` explicitly selects demo expectations and cannot be
combined with `--auth-roundtrip`.

The optional round-trip keeps random credentials/cookies in memory, signs up,
signs out, signs in, checks identity/protected access and signs out again. It
reports a retained unique `@example.test` email, also after an ambiguous network
failure. To clean up, connect privately to your direct database, verify that exact
email and creation time, then delete **only that disposable auth_user row** in a
transaction. Foreign keys cascade its auth accounts/sessions; never delete sample
users or run wildcard cleanup. There is no public account-delete endpoint.

```sql
BEGIN;
SELECT id, email, created_at FROM auth_user WHERE email = :'smoke_email';
-- Confirm this is the one reported disposable account before deleting.
DELETE FROM auth_user WHERE email = :'smoke_email';
COMMIT;
```

Also verify signup/login/logout, current/other-session revocation, concurrent
users, protected app/data access, seeded records, exact origin, Secure/HttpOnly/Lax
cookies, hidden OAuth, cache disabled and a separate binding-free PR preview.
Inspect light/dark desktop/mobile pages for console/hydration errors. Exercise
limiter saturation and deliberate database failures only on isolated local data.
Record your version/revision and redacted results; local tests cannot establish
hosted pooling, TLS, cache or proxy behavior for you.

## 9. Optional OAuth, then rollback and recovery

Launch uses email/password with open signup. To enable providers later, register
Google/GitHub apps with callbacks
`https://<worker-name>.<account-subdomain>.workers.dev/api/auth/callback/google`
and `https://<worker-name>.<account-subdomain>.workers.dev/api/auth/callback/github`.
Add complete `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` or
`GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`/`GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` pairs to your private secrets file,
retaining the existing auth secret, URL and binding. Repeat the complete version
upload/check/promotion workflow. Incomplete pairs remain hidden. Verify real
consent/denial flows on your canonical origin and both auth variants. See
[auth boundaries and limiter limitations](auth.md).

Before every promotion, retain a compatible known-good version and verify its
binding IDs, secret names and schema expectations. If smoke fails:

```bash
npx wrangler rollback <known-good-version-id> --config "$TENBOARDS_DEPLOY_CONFIG" \
  --message 'Revert failed deployment'
npm run deploy:check -- 'https://<worker-name>.<account-subdomain>.workers.dev'
```

Prefer an auth-on rollback. If returning to an older demo, first confirm it has
neither binding nor auth secret, then check with `--demo`. For an initial Hello
World placeholder, verify its original response manually; it cannot pass the
application checker. A different auth secret may invalidate sessions. Never
construct a partial auth/binding rollback.

Worker rollback does **not** reverse migrations, seed upserts or deleted external
resources. Keep needed resources; assess schema compatibility even though shipped
migrations are additive. Restore from your verified Neon recovery point/branch or
backup as a separate operation; stop dependent writes and obtain your deployment
owner's data-recovery approval before replacing live data. See [Cloudflare rollback
constraints](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/versions-and-deployments/rollbacks/).

## Local rehearsal and isolated previews

You can rehearse without Cloudflare or Neon credentials. The supplied Docker
service uses Postgres 17 on port 54329. Choose a unique, test-owned database name:

```bash
docker compose up -d
docker compose exec -T postgres createdb -U tenboards tenboards_readiness_example
export DATABASE_URL='postgresql://tenboards:tenboards_local@127.0.0.1:54329/tenboards_readiness_example'
npm run db:migrate
npm run db:seed
npm run build
npm run check
npm run typecheck
npm run auth:test
npm run data:parity
npm run worker:test
npm run worker:auth
npm run worker:security
node --experimental-strip-types scripts/operations-check.ts
node --experimental-strip-types scripts/deploy-check-test.ts
node --experimental-strip-types scripts/cutover-order-check.ts # local dry-run only
# Stop test servers, then drop only this test-owned database.
unset DATABASE_URL
docker compose exec -T postgres dropdb -U tenboards tenboards_readiness_example
```

The operations check includes deployment-preparation validation, remote opt-in/TLS
rejection without remote connections, repeated migrations/seeds in its own fresh
Docker database, read-only/account smoke and incomplete deployment rejection.
It drops its own database. Node auth and parity tests remain local-only.

Run `npm run dev` without DB/auth configuration and smoke `/dashboard/default`;
`npm run screenshots -- --routes /dashboard/default` captures its four states.
For local Workers, `npm run worker:dev -- --binding` selects `--env local --local`
and an ignored Docker connection; it never uses remote dev.

PR uploads use only `npm run preview:deploy -- --preview-alias pr-NNN` and its
separate demo-only `tenboards-preview` Worker, with ASSETS and no bindings/secrets.
Its guarded config deliberately bypasses your deployment bindings. Keep its remote
inventory empty of secrets and DB access; a version URL of your database Worker
is not a safe substitute. See [contributor rules](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Optional adopter Assistant configuration

See [Assistant setup and limits](assistant.md). The repository demo and previews must have no AI keys. The preview guard rejects all five provider keys, model overrides and `ASSISTANT_ORIGIN`, including blank caller variables; its clean build strips them and remote inventory stays ASSETS-only.

For your own existing DB/auth Worker, `deploy:prepare --secrets-file /absolute/private/path/worker-secrets.json --include-assistant` explicitly opts into copying the documented Assistant keys/models/origin from the private caller environment. Without `--include-assistant`, caller AI variables are never copied. Nonblank values are validated and copied into the exclusive 0600 file, never into build environment, console output or Wrangler vars. `ASSISTANT_ORIGIN`, if supplied, must match the canonical auth URL. The command still only prepares a candidate; it does not upload, provision, migrate or change production. Existing files are never overwritten. Keep provider keys in your secret manager and follow the candidate-review steps above.

Auth-off/no-DB adopters may supply server-only provider bindings to their own deployment without enabling auth or adding a DB. A hosted live configuration needs an explicit HTTPS `ASSISTANT_ORIGIN` and an adopter-owned shared ingress/provider budget if deployed across isolates. The DB/auth-specific preparation helper does not provision this separate mode or establish a global quota. Node uses private process environment. Never run paid acceptance against this repository's live or preview Workers.


## Source: .agents/skills/tenboards-build-ui/references/blocks.md

# Public block contracts

Import from `@/components/blocks`; inspect the TSDoc/source for the exact installed API.
Chart primitives also export from `@/components/blocks/charts`, never import `recharts`
directly in routes. The executable kit is `src/routes/(main)/dashboard/kit/-components/`.

| Block | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| PageHeader | `title: string`, optional `description: string`, `actions`, `className`; one h1 per page |
| DashboardCard | Native Card props plus `density: "compact" | "standard"`; default standard already follows compact responsive tokens |
| SectionHeader | `title`, optional `description`, `actions`, `level: 2 | 3`, `id`; compose inside DashboardCard |
| StatCard | `label: string`, `value: ReactNode`; optional `help`, `trend`, `actions`, `icon`, `density`, `level`, `className` |
| CardContent | Public re-export of the existing card content slot |
| DataTable | Caller-owned `table`, required accessible `label`; optional `empty`, `pagination`, `mobile: "reflow" | "scroll"`, `columnLabels`, `className` |
| DashboardChart | ChartContainer props, including `config` and `children`; default responsive height |
| DashboardTooltip | ChartTooltipContent props; custom formatter replaces the entire row |
| DashboardLegend | Required named-series `config`, optional payload and className |

For tables copy the generator's `./scripts/templates/records-table.tsx.template`:
`ColumnDef<DataTableFeatures, Row>[]`, `useTable({ features: dataTableFeatures, data,
columns, getRowId, initialState })`. Headers are plain labels: DataTable supplies
sorting buttons. `mobile="reflow"` is the default. Use an informative empty state.

Charts use `seriesConfig({ revenue: "Revenue" })`, `chartAxis`, `chartGrid`,
`chartCursor` and `useChartMotion()`. Spread motion onto each mark and Tooltip;
use `config.revenue.color` for marks and preserve labels in custom tooltips.
Copy the generated activity chart's accessible table alternative when changing series.
Use `formatCurrency(value, currency?)`, `formatNumber(value)` and `formatPercent(value)`
for explicit en-US formatting. For chart ticks use `(value) => formatCurrency(value)`;
a chart callback may pass an index as its second argument. Numeric Table columns
use `(a, b, id) => a.getValue<number>(id) - b.getValue<number>(id)`, not a v8 sort name.

Use named layout classes such as `min-w-0 space-y-5`, `grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3`.
Do not copy raw primitive Card/Table markup to imitate blocks or add raw colors,
arbitrary sizing, new density overrides or exceptions to pass a new page.


## Source: .agents/skills/tenboards-build-ui/SKILL.md

---
name: tenboards-build-ui
description: Build tenboards dashboards and app pages with generators and public blocks. Use when adding or changing a dashboard, page, KPI, chart, revenue summary, or data table.
license: MIT
metadata:
  version: "1.0"
---
# Build tenboards UI

Default to the existing compact system and read-only demo data unless the user asks
for live data. Use the generator, then adapt its domain; do not offer a new design system.
Read root AGENTS.md and DESIGN.md. Inspect `/dashboard/kit` and the local component
before composing. If Impeccable is installed, use Operate mode and its craft floor.

## External projects

Inside a tenboards clone, keep using `@/components/blocks`. Only when installing
blocks into another initialized React 19 + Tailwind v4 + shadcn project, use the
kit's registry links and current-host `npx shadcn add` commands. Items install
under `components/tenboards`, include chart helpers and apply the default global
theme/compact CSS. Review that CSS change; retain accessible chart data alternatives.
`/llms.txt` indexes the registry and guidance; resolve its root-relative URLs
against the host from which you fetched it before passing a URL to shadcn.

## Progress checklist

- [ ] Run `npm run new:dashboard <slug>` for metrics/charts or `npm run new:page <slug>`
  for a listing. Both live at `/dashboard/<slug>`; optional `-- --title "Title"` sets the title.
  Generators register sidebar, route catalog and parity reads and reject occupied slugs.
- [ ] Read [block contracts](references/blocks.md) for the blocks you need. Adapt
  generated `-components/`, server types and canonical fixtures together; use realistic
  neutral sample records. Update table headings, accessible labels, empty copy and KPI
  units to match the requested domain. Do not leave generic requests in a Vendors page.
- [ ] Preserve the generated guarded loader and `readSource` boundary. Components
  import types only from the server layer, never fixtures. For a real DB query, use
  `tenboards-connect-data`; clearly retain the illustrative DB TODO until implemented.
- [ ] Run `npm run build`, `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`.
- [ ] Run `npm run check:design` and `npm run verify:page -- /dashboard/<slug>`.
  Use an isolated demo server/port for scratch work, e.g. `--base-url http://127.0.0.1:3404`.
  Read `verify/report.json` and route reports; fix violations/runtime errors and rerun.
- [ ] Inspect the four light/dark × desktop/mobile captures, empty state, keyboard
  controls and reduced motion. Report actual results and any remaining blocker.

## Gotchas

- SSR clocks must share an initial value; live clocks start after hydration. Delayed
  hydration evidence must actually delay scripts, not expire during server startup
  ([review #24](https://github.com/moeghashim/tenboards/pull/24#discussion_r4359849605)).
- A tooltip `formatter` replaces the whole row: preserve series labels as well as
  values ([review #24](https://github.com/moeghashim/tenboards/pull/24#discussion_r4359849593)).
- Compact desktop sizing must not shrink mobile grouped inputs into focus zoom
  ([review #65](https://github.com/moeghashim/tenboards/pull/65#discussion_r4368113744)).
  Keep body/table ≥13px, metadata ≥12px and targets ≥24px per DESIGN.md.
- A login redirect is not a verified dashboard. Check the final route and use the
  intended demo server ([review #78](https://github.com/moeghashim/tenboards/pull/78#discussion_r4375549966)).
- Tokens, not literals or arbitrary typography escapes; new pages get no exception
  ([review #78](https://github.com/moeghashim/tenboards/pull/78#discussion_r4375549973)).
- Framework/API invariants (not invented review findings): route groups add no URL
  segment; never hand-edit `routeTree.gen.ts`; spread `useChartMotion()` on animated
  series/tooltips so SSR and reduced motion stay stable. Use the local Table v9 API,
  not v8 `useReactTable` examples.

### Scratch evaluation corrections (v0.9 / 004)

- The Sales eval initially assumed a third options argument to `formatCurrency`
  and a Table `sortFn: "basic"`. The agent corrected both: the helper accepts only
  `(value, currency?)`; numeric columns use a numeric comparator. Wrap it for chart
  tick callbacks so an index is not passed as the currency argument. Read installed
  signatures before borrowing examples.
- Scratch evaluations with a symlinked `node_modules` hit Nitro dev-runner module
  resolution errors and HTTP 503 before page rendering. Install dependencies inside
  each scratch clone; alternatively build and run `npm run preview -- --port <port>`
  and pass that origin to `verify:page`. This is a harness setup failure, not an
  accessibility pass; preserve the failed report alongside the successful rerun.
- Gitignored scratch TSX probes can still enter `tsc` through tsconfig's include
  patterns. The Sales empty-state probe introduced an unused React import; remove
  temporary probes after verification and rerun typecheck. Gitignore is not a
  TypeScript exclusion.


## Source: .agents/skills/tenboards-connect-data/SKILL.md

---
name: tenboards-connect-data
description: Connect tenboards typed reads to demo fixtures and Postgres with Drizzle. Use when adding a data source, database query, schema migration, seed, parity scenario, or auth-guarded server loader.
license: MIT
metadata:
  version: "1.0"
---
# Connect tenboards data

Preserve the zero-config demo and one typed contract across demo and database reads.
Read [data workflow](references/data-workflow.md) before changing schema, seeds or
server functions. Keep presentation in blocks and route-local components.

## Progress checklist

- [ ] Inspect the owning domain read and generated types/fixture. Define validated
  inputs and one serializable output contract; choose stable IDs and deterministic order.
- [ ] Implement separate demo and DB functions behind `readSource`. Keep fixtures
  server-side. Replace generated DB TODOs with real ordered queries before claiming
  database integration; comparing two fixture clones does not prove DB parity.
- [ ] Add an additive migration and repeatable fixture seed if persistence is needed.
  Never rewrite shipped migration SQL/journal history or overwrite adopter records.
- [ ] Keep `requireSession()` inside each app-data server function before reading data,
  even when its parent route is guarded. Validate inputs at the server boundary.
- [ ] Register all reads/scenarios and run migrations, seed and `npm run data:parity`
  against an explicitly selected disposable local database. Check missing/filter/empty
  cases, deterministic ordering, repeat seeds and date boundaries where relevant.
- [ ] Run build/check/typecheck; verify any affected page with `verify:page` and
  report demo and DB evidence separately. No database access means DB acceptance
  remains unverified; finish independent demo work and report the missing prerequisite.

## Gotchas

- Apply SQL filters before result limits; filtering the first 100 rows in memory
  loses matching records ([review #67](https://github.com/moeghashim/tenboards/pull/67#discussion_r4368227630)).
- Verify the requested page, not a login redirect ([review #78](https://github.com/moeghashim/tenboards/pull/78#discussion_r4375549966)).
- Existing source/auth contracts: configured DB errors remain visible, never fall
  back to fixtures; demo identities are not authenticated users or ownership checks.
  No CRUD, RBAC or authentication changes are implied by adding a typed read.


## Source: src/components/blocks/cards.tsx

```tsx
import { type ComponentProps, type ReactNode, useId } from "react";

import { cn } from "cn";

import { Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardHeader } from "@/components/ui/card";

/** Card surface using the shared compact or standard spacing; compose with UI card slots. */
export type DashboardCardProps = ComponentProps<typeof Card> & {
  /** Compact uses 12px spacing; standard follows responsive card tokens. Defaults to standard. */
  density?: "compact" | "standard";
};

/** Shared dashboard card. All native Card props, children and accessible names pass through. */
export function DashboardCard({ density = "standard", className, ...props }: DashboardCardProps) {
  return <Card {...props} size={density === "compact" ? "sm" : "default"} className={cn("min-w-0", className)} />;
}

/** Props for a card-level semantic heading. */
export interface SectionHeaderProps {
  /** Visible section heading. */
  title: ReactNode;
  /** Supporting content below the heading. */
  description?: ReactNode;
  /** Route-owned controls, wrapping beside the heading. */
  actions?: ReactNode;
  /** Heading hierarchy; defaults to h2. */
  level?: 2 | 3;
  /** Heading ID for aria-labelledby and fragment links. */
  id?: string;
}

/** Wrapping h2/h3 header for DashboardCard, with optional description and actions. */
export function SectionHeader({ title, description, actions, level = 2, id }: SectionHeaderProps) {
  const Heading = level === 2 ? "h2" : "h3";
  return (
    <CardHeader className="flex flex-wrap items-start justify-between gap-3">
      <div className="min-w-0 flex-1 basis-40">
        <Heading id={id} className="text-base font-medium tracking-tight wrap-break-word">
          {title}
        </Heading>
        {description && <div className="text-muted-foreground mt-1 text-sm">{description}</div>}
      </div>
      {actions && <div className="flex max-w-full flex-wrap items-center gap-2">{actions}</div>}
    </CardHeader>
  );
}

/** Props for an accessibly labelled metric card. */
export interface StatCardProps {
  /** Heading hierarchy; defaults to h2. */
  level?: 2 | 3;
  /** Accessible metric name and visible heading. */
  label: string;
  /** Route-formatted metric; units and locale belong to the caller. */
  value: ReactNode;
  /** Supporting explanation below the value. */
  help?: ReactNode;
  /** Text or indicator alongside the value; pair color with a label. */
  trend?: ReactNode;
  /** Route-owned controls in the card header. */
  actions?: ReactNode;
  /** Optional decorative or accessibly named icon. */
  icon?: ReactNode;
  /** Card spacing; defaults to standard. */
  density?: "compact" | "standard";
  /** Additional layout classes. */
  className?: string;
}

/** Metric card with tabular values and optional help, trend, icon and action slots. */
export function StatCard({
  label,
  value,
  help,
  trend,
  actions,
  icon,
  density = "standard",
  level = 2,
  className,
}: StatCardProps) {
  const id = useId();
  const Heading = level === 2 ? "h2" : "h3";
  return (
    <DashboardCard density={density} className={className} role="group" aria-labelledby={id}>
      <CardHeader>
        {icon}
        <Heading id={id} className="text-muted-foreground text-sm font-medium wrap-break-word">
          {label}
        </Heading>
        {actions && <CardAction>{actions}</CardAction>}
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent className="flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-1">
        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
          <div className="min-w-0 text-2xl leading-tight font-medium tracking-tight wrap-break-word tabular-nums xl:text-3xl">
            {value}
          </div>
          {trend}
        </div>
        {help && <div className="text-muted-foreground text-sm">{help}</div>}
      </CardContent>
    </DashboardCard>
  );
}

```

## Source: src/components/blocks/charts.tsx

```tsx
import { type ComponentProps, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";

import { cn } from "cn";

import { ChartContainer, type ChartLegendContent, ChartTooltipContent } from "@/components/ui/chart";

/** Opaque chart colors and distinct line patterns. Skips duplicate Default chart-3. */
export const chartSeries = [
  { color: "var(--chart-1)", strokeDasharray: undefined },
  { color: "var(--chart-2)", strokeDasharray: "6 3" },
  { color: "var(--chart-4)", strokeDasharray: "2 3" },
  { color: "var(--chart-5)", strokeDasharray: "8 3 2 3" },
] as const;

/** Accessible series identity shared by marks, tooltip and legend. */
export interface SeriesStyle {
  /** Human-readable series name. */
  label: string;
  /** CSS token color for marks and legend samples. */
  color: string;
  /** Supplementary line pattern so color is not the only distinction. */
  strokeDasharray?: string;
}

/** Assign shared colors/patterns to named series in insertion order; styles repeat after four series. */
export function seriesConfig<T extends string>(labels: Record<T, string>): Record<T, SeriesStyle> {
  return Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries<string>(labels).map(([key, label], index) => [
      key,
      { label, ...chartSeries[index % chartSeries.length] },
    ]),
  ) as Record<T, SeriesStyle>;
}

/** Recharts axis props: muted 12px ticks without decorative axis lines. */
export const chartAxis = {
  axisLine: false,
  tickLine: false,
  tickMargin: 8,
  tick: { fill: "var(--text-muted)", fontSize: 12 },
} as const;
/** Recharts CartesianGrid props for decorative dashed horizontal separators. */
export const chartGrid = { vertical: false, stroke: "var(--border)", strokeDasharray: "3 3" } as const;
/** Recharts tooltip cursor props using a dashed muted stroke. */
export const chartCursor = { stroke: "var(--text-muted)", strokeDasharray: "3 3" } as const;

/** Format a number using the explicit en-US locale. */
export const formatNumber = (value: number) => new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US").format(value);
/** Format an amount using en-US and the supplied ISO currency (USD by default). */
export const formatCurrency = (value: number, currency = "USD") =>
  new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency, maximumFractionDigits: 2 }).format(value);
/** Format a ratio as an en-US percentage with at most one decimal place. */
export const formatPercent = (value: number) =>
  new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "percent", maximumFractionDigits: 1 }).format(value);

function subscribeMotion(onChange: () => void) {
  const media = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)");
  media.addEventListener("change", onChange);
  return () => media.removeEventListener("change", onChange);
}
// Static SSR and first client paint; enable short animations only after hydration.
/** SSR-safe reduced-motion subscription. Spread onto every animated series and tooltip. */
export function useChartMotion() {
  const reduced = useSyncExternalStore(
```
